- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; increase early-period lows and adjust downward momentum in later periods.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots; apply dampening factor to subsequent days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in long-term (30d) forecasts — if forecast is >2.5x recent high, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag — delay peak forecast until 2–3 days after sentiment shift.
- If sentiment is neutral or flat (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture gradual decline; apply linear decay from recent high to low over 7–10 days.
- Forecast errors are more severe in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is unstable — use sentiment-weighted smoothing for first 5 days.
